endorsements.designation: Preferred; sole listed option for TP53-mutated poor-risk AML
endorsements.indication_text: Relapsed/refractory AML: clinical trial enrollment is the preferred route. For poor-risk AML with TP53 mutation or del(17p), the guideline lists clinical trial and nothing else.

Relapsed/refractory AML after allogeneic HCT: donor lymphocyte infusion and second allogeneic HCT are treatment options for eligible patients; active disease and shorter remission predict worse outcomes, and patients with active disease should be considered for clinical trials.

eligibility_rationale: ECOG 1, curative intent, and a stated acceptance of trials including travel are on file. Eligibility for any specific protocol still turns on that protocol's criteria and on the pending HLA and HA-1/HA-2 typing plus the TP53 and organ-function workup.

relationship_to_targeted_options.note: Every live option in the experimental ranking reaches her through a trial or a protocolised route, from the rank-1 gating workup through CLAG-GO, the second allograft, HA-1 TCR-T, and DLI. This row is the delivery mechanism for those options, not a competitor to them.

rationale: NCCN AML v3.2026 answers this disease state directly: for poor-risk AML with TP53 mutation or del(17p) it lists clinical trial and nothing else, and for relapsed/refractory disease generally it makes trial enrollment the preferred route. The honest reading is that no approved regimen performs well enough here to displace it, and this report says so rather than manufacturing a standard option. ECOG 1, curative intent, and willingness to travel keep her a realistic candidate; which protocols exist for her turns on the pending workup.
notes: NCCN AML v3.2026 (dated 2025-11-24) is the newest version verified for this run; a later release may exist behind the NCCN login and should be re-checked at the next decision point.

option_label: Gemtuzumab ozogamicin, single agent (CD33 antibody-drug conjugate)

endorsements.indication_text: Relapsed or refractory CD33-positive acute myeloid leukemia in adults and in pediatric patients 2 years and older; single-agent fractionated dosing 3 mg/m2 on days 1, 4, and 7.
Relapsed/refractory CD33-positive AML: single-agent gemtuzumab ozogamicin. The drug is absent from the poor-risk induction options while present for favourable and intermediate risk.

eligibility_rationale: CD33 positivity by flow meets the label. No bilirubin or transaminases are documented, and the boxed hepatotoxicity warning matters more than usual in a patient headed toward a second conditioning regimen.
blocking_factors: No baseline liver function on file; boxed warning for hepatotoxicity including veno-occlusive disease, and the risk stacks with a planned second transplant
Best-quality randomised evidence (Hills 2014 IPD meta-analysis) shows no survival benefit in adverse cytogenetics, her exact karyotype group

biomarker_requirement.threshold: CD33-positive by flow cytometry (label); quantitative antigen density not required by label but requested in the case workup

evidence.effect_size: CR 26% (15/57); no grade 3-4 hepatotoxicity and no veno-occlusive disease reported; 7 patients transplanted afterwards; median neutropenia 23 days

evidence.design: individual-patient-data meta-analysis of GO added to induction
evidence.population: Adverse-cytogenetics subgroup, front-line induction setting (read-across, not single-agent salvage)
evidence.effect_size: No survival benefit in adverse cytogenetics: OR 0.99 (95% CI 0.83-1.18, p=0.9)

toxicity_highlights: Veno-occlusive disease / sinusoidal obstruction syndrome (boxed warning), the wrong risk to invite just before second-transplant conditioning
Prolonged myelosuppression in a six-year-old graft; median neutropenia 23 days in the fractionated series

relationship_to_targeted_options.note: Same CD33 payload as the rank-2 CLAG-GO regimen, which stays in the experimental table because the combination is trial-only with no published efficacy in refractory AML. Single-agent GO is the on-label route if the NCT04050280 slot or intensive fitness fails; giving it alone first spends the hepatic and CD33 exposure the rank-2 regimen plans to use.

rationale: Gemtuzumab ozogamicin is the one drug on this page approved for exactly her situation: single-agent use in relapsed or refractory CD33-positive AML in adults, and her blasts are CD33-positive by flow. The expectation has to be priced honestly, because the fractionated schedule gave 26% CR in first relapse with a clean pre-transplant hepatic record, yet ALFA-0701 excluded secondary AML, which is her category, and the 3,325-patient meta-analysis found no survival benefit in adverse cytogenetics (OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.83-1.18). Baseline liver labs come first, since the veno-occlusive disease warning stacks against a planned second conditioning.
notes: Routed to this table by the PI as the approved member of the CD33 class; the two tables split by regulatory maturity, so this row is carried here on its own merits and the trial-only CLAG-GO stays in the experimental ranking. Quantitative CD33 antigen density is already requested in the case workup and would sharpen the expectation either way.

option_label: Second allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplant (HCT2), cytoreduce first

endorsements.indication_text: Relapsed/refractory AML after allogeneic HCT: donor lymphocyte infusion and second allogeneic HCT are treatment options for eligible patients; active disease and shorter remission predict worse outcomes, and patients with active disease should be considered for clinical trials.

eligibility_rationale: The six-year first remission and the related-donor first graft are favourable on the registry axes, but no cardiac, renal, or hepatic numbers exist to choose a conditioning intensity, the marrow stands at roughly 85% blasts, and the sibling's consent to a second collection is unconfirmed.
blocking_factors: No organ-function baseline on file; conditioning intensity cannot be chosen without an ejection fraction and creatinine clearance
Active disease at ~85% marrow blasts; blasts under 27% carry HR 0.53 (95% CI 0.40-0.72) for survival in the registry model, and the worst band sits at 4% +/- 2% at two years
Sibling donor consent for a second collection not yet documented

evidence.population: Second allogeneic HCT after post-transplant relapse of acute leukemia
evidence.effect_size: 2-year OS 37% +/- 6% when the first graft came from a related donor versus 16% +/- 4% after an unrelated first graft

toxicity_highlights: Non-relapse mortality from a second conditioning regimen and graft-versus-host disease; no registry row tabulates it for her fitness band

relationship_to_targeted_options.note: The same option holds rank 3 in the experimental table as a user-stated feature; the tables are additive, so it appears in both. It is the platform on which the rank-4 HA-1 TCR-T consolidation would be delivered, it is sequenced after the rank-2 cytoreduction, and it is the alternative to the rank-5 DLI at the same fork.

rationale: A second allograft from the sibling is the curative-intent destination the case plan is built around, and the ELN 2022 panel keeps second transplant and DLI in play for eligible post-transplant relapses. NCCN attaches no category to a second allograft after post-transplant relapse, the pathway assumes a first transplant, so this is uncovered rather than contraindicated, and the registry evidence behind it is a prognostic model rather than a treatment effect. The stakes are curative, which makes a sequencing error expensive: taking her to conditioning at roughly 85% blasts sits in the worst registry band, so cytoreduction and an organ-function baseline come first.
notes: The absence of an NCCN category here was established in this case's board round and re-checked for this run: NCCN AML v3.2026 orders the donor search at first relapse but grades no second-transplant pathway.

option_label: Hydroxyurea for blast-count control (with leukapheresis if needed)

endorsements.indication_text: AML with hyperleukocytosis or rapidly rising blast counts: hydroxyurea, with leukapheresis where indicated, as temporising cytoreduction while definitive therapy is arranged.

eligibility_rationale: Oral, titratable, and deliverable regardless of the undocumented organ-function numbers; peripheral blasts moving 58% to 82% inside a fortnight are the exact situation the recommendation covers.
toxicity_highlights: Cytopenias and mucocutaneous effects; no disease-modifying activity

relationship_to_targeted_options.note: Several experimental-table protocols carry count ceilings that hydroxyurea is the usual way to reach: CBX-250 wants white cells under 25,000 and the 211At-BC8-B10 protocol wants circulating blasts under 10,000/mm3. It also buys days ahead of the rank-2 cytoreduction without spending any drug class the plan needs later.

rationale: Hydroxyurea with or without leukapheresis is the NCCN-carried supportive measure for blast-count control, and peripheral blasts that moved from 58% to 82% inside a fortnight make it immediately relevant. It changes counts rather than biology and buys days to weeks, not remission. Several downstream protocols also carry count ceilings that hydroxyurea is the usual way to reach.

option_label: Concurrent specialty palliative care and goals-of-care assessment

endorsements.indication_text: Patients with advanced cancer, explicitly including hematologic malignancies and patients on early-phase trials, should be referred to specialty palliative care early and concurrent with active treatment.

eligibility_rationale: Applies to any patient with advanced disease; nothing in the profile blocks it, and the undocumented fitness and goals-of-care assessment is an explicit open item in her own record.
toxicity_highlights: None; concurrent palliative care does not displace disease-directed therapy

relationship_to_targeted_options.note: The fitness and goals-of-care assessment this brings is the same open item the rank-1 workup names, and her preferences file asks that the 0.75 efficacy weighting be revisited once fitness is known. It informs the weighting of every option in both tables without changing any option's eligibility.

rationale: ASCO's 2024 update tells oncology teams to involve specialty palliative care early and alongside active treatment for advanced cancer, hematologic malignancies included, and that holds with curative intent on the table. In this case the fitness and goals-of-care assessment is an explicit open item, and her own preferences file asks that the efficacy weighting be revisited once fitness is known. Concurrent palliative involvement is how that conversation happens without taking anything off the table.

option_label: Donor lymphocyte infusion (DLI) from the HLA-identical sibling, after cytoreduction

endorsements.designation: EBMT best-practice recommendation (Practice Harmonisation and Guidelines Committee with the Cellular Therapy and Immunobiology Working Party)
endorsements.indication_text: Relapse of haematological malignancy after allogeneic HCT: therapeutic DLI, sibling starting dose 1x10^7 CD3+ cells/kg with escalation; framed mainly for MRD-level or cytoreduced disease rather than high-burden overt relapse.

Relapsed/refractory AML after allogeneic HCT: donor lymphocyte infusion and second allogeneic HCT are treatment options for eligible patients; active disease and shorter remission predict worse outcomes, and patients with active disease should be considered for clinical trials.

eligibility_rationale: The sibling donor exists and a late relapse favours response, but DLI into a marrow at roughly 85% blasts sits in the worst registry band, the relapse pattern reads as graft-versus-leukemia escape, and the sibling's consent to a fresh collection is not yet documented.
blocking_factors: Active disease at ~85% blasts; DLI given in aplasia or active disease carried 2-year OS 15% +/- 3% versus 56% +/- 10% in remission or with favourable karyotype
Grade III-IV GVHD after DLI would close the door on HCT2 and on post-transplant cellular consolidation
Relapse pattern consistent with graft-versus-leukemia escape, which tempers re-infusing the same repertoire

evidence.design: retrospective registry comparison, DLI versus no DLI
evidence.population: First haematologic relapse of AML after allogeneic HCT
evidence.effect_size: 2-year OS 21% +/- 3% with DLI versus 9% +/- 2% without (p=0.04); within the DLI group, 15% +/- 3% with active disease versus 56% +/- 10% in remission

toxicity_highlights: Acute and chronic graft-versus-host disease, which is both the mechanism and the toxicity
Marrow aplasia after infusion into a heavily pretreated graft

relationship_to_targeted_options.note: The same option holds rank 5 in the experimental table as a user-stated feature; the tables are additive, so it appears in both. It sits at the same post-cytoreduction fork as HCT2, shares the sibling donor and collection window the rank-4 HA-1 TCR-T needs, and severe GVHD after it would foreclose both.

rationale: The EBMT 2024 best-practice recommendations are the only graded guideline text for post-transplant relapse, and they set therapeutic sibling DLI at a starting dose of 1x10^7 CD3+ cells/kg, written mainly for low-burden or cytoreduced disease; NCCN carries no DLI recommendation at all, and that silence should not be read as endorsement. Schmid's registry puts DLI given with active disease at 15% +/- 3% two-year survival against 56% +/- 10% in remission, and she stands at roughly 85% blasts today. It stays live as the lower-intensity graft-versus-leukemia route after cytoreduction, particularly if the fitness workup rules out a second conditioning regimen.

option_label: Intensive salvage chemotherapy (high-dose cytarabine-based, e.g. MEC or CLAG-M)

endorsements.indication_text: Relapsed/refractory AML in patients who are candidates for aggressive therapy: high-dose cytarabine-based salvage regimens (cladribine- or fludarabine-containing, MEC and peers), typically as a bridge to transplant.
Relapsed/refractory AML: intensive salvage for fit patients aiming at remission and transplant; trials preferred where available.

eligibility_rationale: The disease state fits the guideline entry, but she has already progressed through FLAG-IDA plus venetoclax, a member of the same high-dose cytarabine and purine-analog family, and no organ-function numbers exist to price another intensive cycle.
blocking_factors: Refractory to FLAG-IDA plus venetoclax; nucleoside and HiDAC cross-resistance caps the expected depth of response
Organ function undocumented; prolonged aplasia in a six-year-old graft could end the transplant plan rather than enable it

evidence.effect_size: Second-line intensive salvage CR rates generally 20-40%, lower after failure of a prior high-dose cytarabine regimen; used here as a cytoreductive bridge rather than a destination

toxicity_highlights: Prolonged grade 4 cytopenias, febrile neutropenia, and infection
Cumulative anthracycline and cardiac exposure on top of prior idarubicin, with no ejection fraction on file

relationship_to_targeted_options.note: Rank-2 CLAG-GO is the trial-delivered member of this same regimen family; an off-protocol CLAG-M or MEC uses the same window, the same marrow reserve, and the same hepatic budget. The choice between them is a delivery-route question, not a different strategy.

rationale: High-dose cytarabine-based salvage (MEC, CLAG-M and peers) is what NCCN lists for relapsed/refractory AML in aggressive-therapy candidates, and it is the standard way to bring a marrow down toward transplant. She has already progressed through FLAG-IDA plus venetoclax, a regimen from the same family, so cross-resistance caps the expected depth and the guideline entry is a partial match to a patient one intensive failure further along. Its role here is cytoreduction toward the curative platform rather than a destination in itself.

option_label: Hypomethylating agent, lower intensity (azacitidine or decitabine)

endorsements.indication_text: Relapsed/refractory AML, less-intensive therapy: azacitidine or decitabine.

eligibility_rationale: Deliverable without the organ-function documentation an intensive regimen needs; nothing in the profile blocks a hypomethylating agent.

evidence.population: Relapsed/refractory AML treated with azacitidine or decitabine
evidence.effect_size: CR 11%, CR/CRi 16%; median OS 6.7 months (95% CI 6.1-7.3); more than 5% circulating blasts predicted worse response and survival

toxicity_highlights: Cytopenias and infection over repeated cycles
Weeks-per-cycle kinetics against a marrow that moved 58% to 82% inside a fortnight

relationship_to_targeted_options.note: An HMA course spends the same weeks the rank-2 cytoreduction would use, so choosing it is a tempo decision against an 85% blast marrow. Adding venetoclax to it would re-expose a drug she has already progressed through, which is the same objection the board logged against venetoclax-containing trial arms.

rationale: Azacitidine or decitabine is the NCCN-listed lower-intensity option for relapsed/refractory AML, and it stays deliverable if fitness closes the intensive route. The honest numbers are poor: CR 11% and median OS 6.7 months (95% CI 6.1-7.3) in the largest reported R/R cohort, with more than 5% circulating blasts predicting worse, and hers are 82%. The approved azacitidine-venetoclax combination does not transfer either, because its label covers newly diagnosed patients unfit for intensive induction and she has already progressed on venetoclax.
notes: US azacitidine and decitabine labels cover MDS rather than relapsed/refractory AML, so the standard-of-care footing here is the NCCN listing, not the label.

option_label: Radiotherapy to the right-thigh extramedullary myeloid sarcoma

endorsements.designation: ILROG consensus guideline (International Lymphoma Radiation Oncology Group)
endorsements.indication_text: Extramedullary leukemia / chloroma: radiotherapy for symptomatic lesions, sites with inadequate response to systemic therapy, or local control; modest doses, commonly around 24 Gy.
endorsements.version_or_date: ILROG 2018 (Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys 102:314-319)

endorsements.indication_text: Myeloid sarcoma: systemic therapy is primary; radiotherapy for symptomatic or bulky lesions or inadequate local control. Coverage of extramedullary AML in the pathway is brief.

eligibility_rationale: A defined soft-tissue limb target on MRI is deliverable regardless of marrow burden or the undocumented organ-function numbers; it treats the thigh site only.
toxicity_highlights: Local skin and soft-tissue reaction, fatigue
No effect on the dominant marrow disease

relationship_to_targeted_options.note: Marrow-directed conditioning does not treat the thigh lesion, a gap the board named against the rank-3 transplant plan, and whether a CD33-directed regimen reaches it is an open question in the rank-2 row (paired series detect CD33 in about 79% of lesions). Radiotherapy to a limb site can run in parallel without spending any systemic option.

rationale: Guideline coverage of extramedullary AML is thin: NCCN mentions radiotherapy for myeloid sarcoma only in passing, and the most specific text is the 2018 ILROG consensus, which supports modest-dose radiotherapy, commonly around 24 Gy, for symptomatic lesions or sites systemic therapy fails to control. The right-thigh lesion is an adverse feature that marrow-directed conditioning would not treat, so the local plan deserves its own line in the sequence. Radiotherapy to a limb site can run alongside systemic therapy without spending any systemic option.

endorsements.indication_text: Relapsed/refractory AML in aggressive-therapy candidates: fludarabine plus high-dose cytarabine and G-CSF with idarubicin, with or without venetoclax.

prior_exposure_note: Given as reinduction for the relapsed/refractory AML. Best response was progressive disease: the marrow rose to about 85% blasts, peripheral blasts moved from 58% to 82%, and an extramedullary right-thigh lesion is present. Refractoriness to this high-dose cytarabine, purine-analog, and venetoclax regimen is why neither venetoclax nor a FLAG-type backbone is offered back as a fresh option.

relationship_to_targeted_options.note: The venetoclax exposure already on record is what narrows several experimental-table routes: the tagraxofusp trial cohort needs a venetoclax washout, the rezatapopt mechanism wanted venetoclax as its killing partner, and the BMS-986497 triplet arm would re-expose it. The foreclosure has already happened; this row records it.

rationale: FLAG-IDA with venetoclax is a standard high-intensity salvage for fit relapsed/refractory AML, and it was the reinduction this patient received. It failed, with progression to an 85% blast marrow and extramedullary spread. It is recorded so the report reads honestly about why no venetoclax-containing or FLAG-type regimen is offered back as a fresh option.

endorsements.indication_text: Relapsed or refractory acute leukemia with a KMT2A translocation (adults and pediatric patients 1 year and older), and relapsed/refractory AML with a susceptible NPM1 mutation.
Relapsed/refractory AML with a KMT2A rearrangement or an NPM1 mutation.

eligibility_rationale: Her karyotype shows KMT2A amplification, a copy-number gain of four copies, not the KMT2A translocation the label and companion diagnostic require, and the disease is NPM1 wild-type.
blocking_factors: KMT2A amplification is a copy-number gain, not the translocation / rearrangement the approval requires
NPM1 wild-type, so the second indication is also unmet

biomarker_requirement.threshold: KMT2A translocation/rearrangement OR susceptible NPM1 mutation

evidence.population: KMT2A-rearranged relapsed/refractory acute leukemia (not this patient's genotype)
evidence.effect_size: CR+CRh 22.8% (95% CI 12.7-35.8) in efficacy-evaluable patients; ORR 63.2%

toxicity_highlights: Differentiation syndrome and QTc prolongation, the menin-inhibitor class effects

relationship_to_targeted_options.note: Named to close the loop on the KMT2A-amplification versus KMT2A-rearrangement distinction, a common misread of this karyotype. It does not interact with the ranked options.

rationale: Revumenib is approved for relapsed/refractory acute leukemia with a KMT2A translocation and for NPM1-mutant disease, and it is named here because her karyotype invites the misread: KMT2A amplification is a copy-number gain of four copies, not the rearrangement the label and its companion diagnostic require, and the disease is NPM1 wild-type. Menin inhibition depends on the dependency a KMT2A fusion or an NPM1 mutation creates, which amplification does not. Assessed and set aside on genotype.

endorsements.indication_text: Adults with relapsed or refractory AML with a susceptible NPM1 mutation.
Relapsed/refractory AML with a susceptible NPM1 mutation.

eligibility_rationale: The disease is NPM1 wild-type, and the ziftomenib approval is restricted to susceptible NPM1 mutations. KMT2A amplification does not create the menin dependency the drug exploits.
blocking_factors: NPM1 wild-type; the approval is restricted to susceptible NPM1 mutations
KMT2A amplification is a copy-number gain and does not confer menin-inhibitor sensitivity
toxicity_highlights: Differentiation syndrome, the menin-inhibitor class effect

relationship_to_targeted_options.note: Listed alongside revumenib so the report is explicit that the approved menin-inhibitor class does not apply to an NPM1-wild-type, KMT2A-amplified genotype. It does not interact with the ranked options.

rationale: Ziftomenib is the second approved menin inhibitor, but its label is confined to relapsed/refractory AML with a susceptible NPM1 mutation, and this disease is NPM1 wild-type. As with revumenib, the KMT2A amplification here is a copy-number gain rather than the fusion that would create menin-inhibitor sensitivity. The drug is approved but the target is absent, so it is assessed and set aside.
notes: pmid:41653248 is the first-approval review (Drugs, 2026) confirming the 2025-11-13 US approval and its NPM1-restricted indication; KOMET-001 trial figures were not re-verifiable for this run and are deliberately not quoted.

option_label: Best supportive care and hospice referral

endorsements.indication_text: Relapsed/refractory AML: best supportive care, including transfusion support, infection management, and hospice, where disease-directed therapy is not deliverable or not wanted.

Relapsed/refractory AML after allogeneic HCT: donor lymphocyte infusion and second allogeneic HCT are treatment options for eligible patients; active disease and shorter remission predict worse outcomes, and patients with active disease should be considered for clinical trials.

eligibility_rationale: Available to any patient; carried here as the standard alternative if the curative pathway proves undeliverable or is declined once fitness and goals are documented.
toxicity_highlights: None from the strategy itself; the trade-off is forgoing disease-directed therapy

relationship_to_targeted_options.note: The path taken if the curative transplant and cellular pathway closes; it does not compete with any single ranked option.

rationale: Best supportive care with transfusion support, infection management, and hospice referral is a named management strategy in relapsed/refractory AML, not a footnote. Curative intent is on file and fitness is not yet documented, so this sits at the next decision point rather than now. It becomes the primary path if the transplant and cellular plan proves undeliverable or unwanted once fitness and goals are on the table.

endorsements.indication_text: IPSS-R high / very-high risk MDS: allogeneic HCT is the potentially curative therapy for eligible patients.
endorsements.version_or_date: NCCN MDS (carried across versions; not re-verified at version level for this run)

endorsements.indication_text: Relapsed/refractory AML after allogeneic HCT: donor lymphocyte infusion and second allogeneic HCT are treatment options for eligible patients; active disease and shorter remission predict worse outcomes, and patients with active disease should be considered for clinical trials.

prior_exposure_note: HLA-identical sibling PBSC allograft around 2020 for RCMD, IPSS-R high/very-high MDS. Best response was complete remission, held for about 72 months. The relapse roughly six years later reads as graft-versus-leukemia escape rather than graft failure, which is part of why a second transplant and post-transplant cellular consolidation are under discussion.
rationale: The first matched-sibling allograft was the curative-intent standard for the high-risk MDS that preceded this AML, and it held a complete remission for about six years. It is logged so the record reads as a complete account rather than one that omits the transplant the current plan builds on. Its durable graft-versus-leukemia effect, and the eventual escape from it, shape the case for a second graft and for antigen-directed consolidation.

endorsements.indication_text: Newly diagnosed therapy-related AML or AML with myelodysplasia-related changes in adults and pediatric patients 1 year and older.
Newly diagnosed AML with myelodysplasia-related changes or therapy-related AML, induction in fit patients.

eligibility_rationale: The histology, AML-MR, matches the label, but the line does not: CPX-351 is approved for newly diagnosed disease and she is relapsed and refractory after a transplant. Prior idarubicin also adds cumulative anthracycline exposure.
blocking_factors: Approved for newly diagnosed AML-MRC / t-AML only; the patient is relapsed/refractory
Prior anthracycline (idarubicin) exposure with no ejection fraction on file
rationale: CPX-351 is the standard intensive frontline choice for the AML-MR histology she carries, which is why a reader would look for it here. The approval and the NCCN listing are confined to newly diagnosed disease, and she is relapsed and refractory after a transplant, so the histology match does not open the drug at this line. It is assessed and set aside on line, not on target.
